title: Ceramics properties table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 9 (Ceramics properties table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 9: About ceramics: properties and uses. To understand how the properties of ceramics make them suited to their uses

questions.q: Explain why porcelain is used for insulators on power lines.
questions.a: It is an electrical insulator, so current cannot flow through it to the pylon; it is also weather resistant.
questions.model: Property: electrical insulator. Use: holds live cables on metal pylons. Link: current cannot pass through the porcelain into the pylon. So porcelain keeps the pylon safe.

questions.q: Hard or tough: a ceramic plate?
Why are ceramics used to line ovens and kilns?
questions.a: High melting point and thermal insulators.

questions.q: Core: Make a table of five ceramic objects at home (mug, plate, tile, sink, brick): property used and why.
questions.a: For example: mug: hard, waterproof, insulator; tile: hard, easy to clean, heat resistant.
questions.model: Teacher fills the first row: mug: hard, waterproof when glazed, poor conductor so the handle stays cool.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why ceramics shatter but metals bend (portal response box).
questions.a: Ceramic particles are held rigidly and cannot slide, so cracks spread; metal layers can slide, so metals bend.

questions.q: Stretch: Why are ceramic tiles used on the underside of some spacecraft?
questions.a: They withstand extreme temperatures on re-entry and are excellent thermal insulators.

questions.q: Big question: why is a ceramic mug hard but easy to smash?
questions.a: Ceramics resist scratching but their particles cannot slide, so they crack and shatter.
